Typical path: study safety engineering, occupational hygiene, or a related science or engineering field -> earn qualifications such as Registered Safety Engineer -> start as a corporate safety officer or assistant -> gain on-site experience and advance to safety supervisor, EHS manager, or third-party consultant.

Best suited to rigorous, principled people who stand firm and communicate well. If you can see risks where everyone else sees no problem and still insist on corrective action, this field has a place for you.

Occupational health and safety specialists and technicians identify, assess, and control workplace health and safety risks. They inspect hazards, provide safety training, investigate accidents, review compliance, and help employers implement occupational safety and health management.

paragraphs: A typical day starts with a checklist inspection of a workshop or construction site, photographing and recording problems and issuing corrective-action orders. The afternoon brings safety training for new employees or preparation of risk-assessment reports. Before inspections or after an accident, staff can work overnight completing materials and supporting investigations.
